validity.recommendation: keep the row; apply the corrected capacity, owners, operator, FuelSource and pressure from fills[]
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: beyond doubt. Alaska LNG is a FERC-certificated project - 171 FERC para 61,134, Docket CP17-178-000, issued 2020-05-21, authorizing 'an approximately 806.9-mile-long, 42-inch-diameter pipeline (Mainline Pipeline)' from the Prudhoe Bay gas treatment plant to liquefaction facilities in the Nikiski area - with a US Department of the Interior right-of-way grant (2020-07-23), a DOE/FECM export authorization (Docket 14-96-LNG, Orders 3554 and 3643-A) under which the project files semi-annual progress reports, a live developer site, and its own row in every EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release since May 2018. CLASSIFICATION: correct as 'transmission' and 'Gas' - an 807-mile 42-inch trunk with eight compressor stations (344,000 hp) and in-state interconnection points, not gathering or distribution. I opened 12 of this row's 26 harvested gem.wiki citations. Unreadable or unusable: the arlis.org AKLNG DEIS (confirmed 404, and it was carrying two cells), eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php (a navigation page the brief bans and which states nothing about this row), the bit.ly/2sgPhVB shortener (resolves to eenews.net/stories/1060053123/, which returns 403 - not citable), the Wayback RDC presentation (200 but image-only, no text layer), naturalgasintel.com (403 bot wall), and the paywalled WSJ/Bloomberg Law items. Net result: SIX of the seventeen units were resting on a dead link or on EIA's navigation page, and all six are now re-sourced to the FERC order, the applicant's Resource Report No. 1, the developer's site, Interior, or a dated EIA release.

Capacity 3,500 MMcf/d is unsupported by any source I could verify. It is an EIA legacy figure: EIA carried 3500 from its May 2018 release through Apr 2025 and revised it to 3300 from the Jul 2025 release onward, and the sheet's ref for the cell was EIA's data.php navigation page, which states nothing. The applicant's own engineering document says otherwise - AKLNG FERC Resource Report No. 1 (April 14, 2017): 'The Mainline is designed for a maximum allowable operating pressure (MAOP) of 2,075 psig and an average stream day rate of 3.1 BSCF/D, and a 3.3 BSCF/D peak capacity' - and the current developer site says 'a daily capacity of 3.3 billion cubic feet'. The 3.9 Bcf/day in the FERC order belongs to the gas treatment plant ('three parallel treatment trains, each sized to process roughly 1.3 BSCF/D'), not to the pipeline, and must not be read onto this row.

EIA moved its operator name to '8 Star Alaska LLC' in the Aug 2026 release. AggregateOwners on the same tab needs the matching correction.

validity.researcher_notes: FuelSource reads 'North Slope Borough', which is an Alaska administrative borough - a place, not a gas source. validity.recommendation: no merge - keep P0147, P0293 and P6534 as separate rows; record P6534 as an AKLNG component and P0293 as the abandoned rival in-state plan
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION for the Alaska cluster, which the brief flags as easy to conflate. (1) P6534 Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Pipeline (63 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMcf/d) IS part of the same FERC application but is NOT a duplicate of P0147 - it is a physically distinct feeder line. The FERC order authorises, as separate facilities, '62.5 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline on the North Slope, which will [run] from the Point Thomson Unit gas production facility to the Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant (Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Line)' and '1.0 miles of 60-inch-diameter pipeline ... (Prudhoe Bay Unit Gas Transmission Line)', alongside the 806.9-mile Mainline. Resource Report No. 1 gives the Point Thomson line its own specs - 62.5 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMSCF/D average stream day rate, 920 MMSCF/D peak, MAOP 1,150 psig - which match P6534's sheet values exactly, so P6534 is correctly and independently recorded. The relationship should be NAMED (P6534 is AKLNG's Point Thomson lateral; Glenfarne's Phase One 'may also include the 63-mile, 32-inch Point Thomson Lateral Pipeline'), and P0147's 807 mi must stay Mainline-only so the two rows do not double-count. Note also that the 60-inch, 1-mile Prudhoe Bay Unit line appears to have no GEM row at all. (2) P0293 Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline (ASAP) is NOT the same project as P0147 and has not been folded into AKLNG Phase One, despite sharing a sponsor (AGDC), a corridor and a North-Slope-to-Southcentral purpose. EIA's Historical Projects sheet keeps ASAP as its own row with different physical specs - 737 mi, '12,36' inch, 500 MMcf/d, $9,970M, status 'On Hold' - and describes it as 'a buried in-state natural gas pipeline ... considered to be the backup plan to the Alaska LNG project', terminating at 'the ENSTAR system near Point Mackenzie in the Mat-Su Valley', not Nikiski. AKLNG Phase One is a 739-mile 42-inch line under FERC docket CP17-178 held by 8 Star Alaska LLC; ASAP is a separate, dormant state project. Different diameter, different capacity, different terminus, different authorisation - two rows, correctly. (3) P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project (TransCanada/ExxonMobil, FERC PF09-11) and P0174 Denali (BP/ConocoPhillips, FERC PF08-26) are 1,126-1,700 mile Alaska Highway export lines to Alberta from an earlier era, already adjudicated as distinct in their own shards; nothing in AKLNG's record folds either into P0147, and I have not merged anything.

cross_row_leads.facts: 171 FERC para 61,134 (CP17-178-000, 2020-05-21) authorises, as part of Alaska LNG, '62.5 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline on the North Slope, which will [run] from the Point Thomson Unit gas production facility to the Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant (Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Line)' - i.e. P6534's 63 mi / 32-inch is AKLNG's Point Thomson lateral, correctly a separate row. The same order authorises a THIRD line with no apparent GEM row: '1.0 miles of 60-inch-diameter pipeline ... (Prudhoe Bay Unit Gas Transmission Line)'. Owner/operator for P6534 should track P0147's: 8 Star Alaska LLC (Glenfarne 75% / AGDC 25%) since 2025-04-18.

AKLNG FERC Resource Report No. 1 (April 14, 2017) gives the Point Thomson lateral its own specs, matching P6534's sheet values: 'approximately 62.5-mile, 32-inch-diameter aboveground pipeline ... average stream day rate of 865 million standard cubic feet per day (MMSCF/D), a peak capacity of 920 MMSCF/D, and an MAOP of 1,150 psig'. So P6534 Pressure = 1,150 psig (NOT the Mainline's 2,075 psig) and its 865 MMcf/d is an average-day, not peak, figure. The Prudhoe Bay Unit line is separately described as 'approximately 1-mile, 60-inch-diameter ... average stream day rate of 2.8 BSCF/D, a peak capacity of 4.0 BSCF/D and a MAOP of 720 psig'.

Alaska LNG Project LLC semi-annual report to DOE/FECM, April 1, 2026: 'Phase One consists of an approximately 739-mile, 42-inch pipeline constructed in three to four sections, or spreads. Phase One may also include the 63-mile, 32-inch Point Thomson Lateral Pipeline which will give the pipeline access to gas from the Point Thomson Unit.' P6534's status should track AKLNG's - proposed, Pre-FID, and only conditionally in Phase One.

EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, May 2026 release (also Aug 2026), sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' Excel row 1186: 'Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline Project (ASAP) also known as North Slope to Central Alaska Pipeline', operator Alaska Gasline Development Corp, status 'On Hold', in-service 'na', 737 mi, diameter '12,36', 500 MMcf/d, $9,970M, row last updated 2021-04-09; project note: 'The proposed Alaska Stand Alone Gas Pipeline project (ASAP) is a buried in-state natural gas pipeline designed to provide long term stable natural gas supplies to Alaskans and is considered to be the backup plan to the Alaska LNG project. The ASAP project consists of a Gas Conditioning Facility on the North Slope and a 700-mile pipeline that ties into the ENSTAR system near Point Mackenzie in the Mat-Su Valley.' This is the source that keeps P0293 and P0147 apart: different diameter, capacity, terminus and authorisation, and EIA has not updated the ASAP row since 2021 - relevant to P0293's shelved-vs-cancelled dormancy call.

alaska-lng.com newsroom lists 'GLENFARNE AND DONLIN GOLD SIGN LETTER OF INTENT FOR ALASKA GAS AND INFRASTRUCTURE, JANUARY 7, 2026 - Agreement Encompasses Natural Gas Supply, Pipeline and Power Plant'. That is dated evidence NEWER than P2526's LastUpdated of 2025-09-16 and bears directly on whether the Donlin Gold mine gas pipeline is still live and how it would be supplied - a Donlin line fed off AKLNG rather than from Cook Inlet would change P2526's FuelSource and endpoints.

The Alaska LNG record contains nothing that revives or re-scopes the older Alaska Highway export projects: the DOE/FECM semi-annual report traces AKLNG's own lineage from the September 2014 FERC pre-filing (PF14-21) through CP17-178 and the 2025 Glenfarne transfer, with no reference to the TransCanada/ExxonMobil Alaska Pipeline Project. Confirms the existing boundary between P0146/P0174 and P0147; no merge.

summary: Alaska LNG is real, correctly classified and still proposed (FERC-certificated 2020, Glenfarne-led since 2025, no FID as of mid-2026); six of seventeen units rested on a dead arlis.org DEIS link or EIA's banned data.php navigation page and are re-sourced, and the pass corrects Capacity 3500 -> 3300 MMcf/d, ownership AGDC 100% -> Glenfarne 75% / AGDC 25% with operator 8 Star Alaska LLC, FuelSource 'North Slope Borough' -> Prudhoe Bay Unit / Point Thomson Unit, and fills Pressure 2,075 psig; P0293 ASAP and P6534 Point Thomson are adjudicated as NOT duplicates of this row.
